//: The combined runtime's machine-readable layering contract.
Before consolidation the package manager made a forbidden layer edge
require a manifest edit. Inside one package this file and lint:layers
`mayImport` is exhaustive: a directory may import from itself and from the
layers listed, and from nothing else. Layer names are directory paths, so
the ordering INSIDE global is enforced too -- math is not allowed to reach
sideways into model just because both are global.

why: Carbon imageio (E:/carbonengine/imageio): CPU image containers shared by the
resource layer (texture pipeline, image handlers) and the abstraction layer
(Tr2BitmapDimensions describes every AL texture). Classes only; the
handlers that call format readers live in resource/imageio.
Contract roots use schema implementation metadata so required
methods carry @impl.abstract as well as their throwing body.
Dependency-free enum storage shared by schema and Blue; never imports either facade.
Ports of Carbon's blueexposure layer - facilities Blue provides to every
subsystem rather than to one. BlueScriptCallback is used by Carbon's audio,
ResMan, BluePython and Trinity UI alike, so its port cannot live with any
single consumer, and cannot live in core, which nothing below may import.
Donor classes written but deliberately NOT live: every one carries its
`// Source:` line and the reason it was dropped. They exist so the decision
is recorded at a readable place instead of only as a lint baseline entry.
trinity and resource keep theirs under their own layer; global has no
layer of its own, so its dropped tree is declared here.

//: Trinity MAY import resource, and importing one Res class has never been
the problem - resource/texture/** reaches only consts, imageio and the
payload validators. Preferring the FILE over resource/index.js is a
nicety, not a rule: the root barrel pulls CjsResMan, the worker loaders
and every format reader, which a bundler mostly shakes out again. It
would only matter to someone wanting the audio engine without trinity.
The rule in the other direction is real: resource may NOT import
trinity, so a resource cannot reach a render context. That is why a
texture is created on first bind (Tr2ImageIOHelpers.RealizeTexture)
rather than in DoPrepare as Carbon does.

why: Carbon's abstraction layer, a sibling of trinity rather than a part of it
(namespace TrinityALImpl, target TrinityAL_stub). It is the resource and
context family a backend implements, so it sits BELOW trinity and imports
no trinity, resource, core or tools.
SOF is standalone and trinity is NOT in its list, which is the whole
point of writing this down. SOF emits a graph that names Trinity and
audio classes; naming a class is not importing it, and a consumer
supplies the constructors. The day someone 'just imports Trinity here'
the build fails instead of the property quietly disappearing.
The implemented abstraction-layer backend extends canonical dependency-floor,
and Trinity contracts. It never imports core, tools, or another backend.
Composition. It is allowed to know about everything below it, which is
exactly why nothing below is allowed to know about it.
Acquisition only. The demo suite left for the separate
carbonenginejs/demos repository on 2026-08-30, taking the market,
Show Info, Ship Tree, chat, diagram and demo-host families with it;
the realtime wire contract followed once the server lived there too,
and per-object tooling was retired to trinity documentation.
mayImport is exhaustive, so narrowing it IS the enforcement. Anything
here that needs resource, trinity, or core is not a tool -- it is either
a demo, which belongs in the demos repository, or a runtime value that
belongs lower down.
